root_cause.text: In iomap_read_folio_iter(), the ownership handoff of a folio without an iomap_folio_state (ifs) to the IO helper was incorrectly gated solely on whether the entire folio had been submitted (*bytes_submitted == folio_len), but when the I/O granularity is smaller than the block size (1 << i_blkbits equals folio size), partial folio submissions occur, causing the condition to fail and resulting in a double completion via iomap_read_end().
root_cause.evidence: The commit description explains that the previous fix (aa35dd5cbc06) "did not handle the case where 1 << inode->i_blkbits matches the folio size but is different from the granularity used for the IO, which means IO can be submitted for less than the full folio for the !ifs case." It further states that when this occurs, the condition `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;` will not invalidate `ctx->cur_folio`, leading to `iomap_read_end()` being called on a folio already owned by the IO helper. The patch replaces the condition with an unconditional check for !ifs to always hand off ownership in that case.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit fixes the vulnerability by ensuring that if all bytes of a folio without ifs are submitted to the IO helper, ctx->cur_folio is set to NULL to prevent further access. In iomap_read_folio, iomap_read_end is only called if cur_folio is not NULL. In iomap_read_end for !ifs, it now asserts that bytes_submitted is 0, preventing double completion. These changes eliminate the root cause of double completion when partial submissions occur for folios without ifs.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit applies the fix for the vulnerability: it removes the +1 bias in read_bytes_pending tracking, corrects the logic in iomap_read_end to only handle folios without ifs when no bytes were submitted, and sets ctx->cur_folio = NULL in iomap_read_folio_iter when the entire folio has been submitted to the IO helper. Additionally, iomap_read_folio now checks ctx->cur_folio before calling iomap_read_end. These changes prevent the double completion and invalid folio access described in the root cause.
